slides.title: Delegating to Subgenerators with yield from
slides.prompt: The 'yield from' syntax allows a generator to delegate part of its operations to another generator or iterable. It simplifies nested loops and transparently establishes a bi-directional channel between caller and subgenerator.
slides.codeSnippet:
def subgen():
    yield 'A'
    yield 'B'

def main_gen():
    yield 1
    yield from subgen()
    yield 2

print(list(main_gen())) # Outputs [1, 'A', 'B', 2]

slides.title: Capturing Return Values from Subgenerators
slides.prompt: How does `yield from` handle a return statement value inside a subgenerator?
options: The return value of the subgenerator becomes the value of the `yield from` expression
The return value is ignored completely
It yields the returned value to the outer caller automatically
slides.correctAnswer: The return value of the subgenerator becomes the value of the `yield from` expression

slides.title: Exception Delegation in yield from
slides.prompt: How are exceptions sent via throw() or close() handled during yield from delegation?
options: They are passed directly through to the active subgenerator
They are swallowed and suppressed by default
They cause an immediate UnhandledException crash in caller
They restart the main delegating generator
slides.correctAnswer: They are passed directly through to the active subgenerator
